_why: Questions verified DEFECTIVE by working the problem, not by a structural rule. Each one was extracted cleanly enough to pass every automated gate — four options, a key letter that exists, numbers agreeing across languages — and is still wrong on the page. The only way to find these is to solve them, so the finding is recorded here rather than re-discovered by the next reviewer.
_how: paper_common.excluded() reads this; the builders skip anything listed. Add to it as review turns up more — Rohan's findings belong here too.
_note: Most cluster in complex-LaTeX maths (nested surds, telescoping series). That is a signal about the EXTRACTION, not the commission's papers: where a stem carried heavy LaTeX, the transcription lost structure while still looking plausible.

excluded.reason: No option is correct. Stem is a = √(11+√3), b = √(12+√2), c = √(6+√4) → a≈3.568, b≈3.662, c≈2.828, so b > a > c. The four options are 'a>b>c', 'c>a>b', 'a>b<c', 'a<c>b' — none of which is that. Key says C ('a>b<c'), and both of its claims are false.

Stem lost its structure in extraction. As printed it reads 1/√9 + 1/√11 + ... + 1/√2025, which sums to no option. The original is the telescoping series 1/(√9+√11) + 1/(√11+√13) + ... = (√2025-√9)/2 = 21 — which is exactly the keyed answer D. The KEY is right; the visible question is unanswerable.
√1375 + √1125 − √1375 = √1125 = 15√5, which is IRRATIONAL (option B). Key says C (Rational). Either the key or the stem is wrong; either way it cannot be served.
Stem defines b and c as the SAME expression ((√6+√5)/5), so the comparison it asks for is ill-posed. Extraction damage.
Incoherent stem: 'If x = r, then find the value of r = x, and the discount = r, z, then find the value of ___'. Not a question.
Match-the-columns with Column II truncated — only entries 1 and 2 survive extraction, so the student cannot see what 3 and 4 are and no option can be justified.

Stem and answer do not correspond. 'If one task can be done in 24 days, how many days to complete 30 tasks?' with keyed answer 13/3 days. The Hindi is garbled differently again ('30 दिनों में कितने दिन लगेंगे'). Whatever the original asked, this is not recoverable from what was extracted.

Garbled stem: 'इसमें कौन-सा भौतिक संज्ञान नहीं है ?' ('which physical cognition is not in this') with options जल / चाय / ध्वनि / प्रमाण. Almost certainly 'भौतिक परिवर्तन' (physical change) in the original; as extracted it is not a question.

The two languages carry DIFFERENT options: English −5/7, 29, 9, −11 versus Hindi −5/7, −42, −14, 28. The keyed letter D is the greatest in the Hindi list (28) but not in the English one (−11), so the same paper gives two different right answers depending on which half the student reads.

Arithmetic does not reach any option: ₹1,728 less 25% = 1,296, plus 20% = 1,555.20, but the options are 1,500/1,620/1,664/1,665. 1,296 x 1.25 = 1,620 = the keyed answer, so the extraction almost certainly turned a 25% increase into 20%.
Key contradicts the arithmetic. A beats B by 270 in 900 (B runs 630) and beats C by 340 (C runs 560); when B runs 900, C runs 800, so B beats C by 100 — option D. The key says B (70).
Marked price ₹810 with 8% VAT gives ₹874.80, which is not an option. 750 x 1.08 = 810, so the question actually asks for the price BEFORE VAT; the stem as extracted is inverted.
Gibberish: 'विज्ञान फ़लाट का संक्षेप किस क्षेत्र से है?' / 'Which area is the summary of the science flat from?' with options Physics / Qualitative science / Chair / Fact.
45 items at ₹49 makes 35 items ₹38.11, but the key says ₹63 — which is what you get from 35 items at ₹49 scaled to 45. The two quantities are swapped in the extracted stem.
15% of ₹2,500 is ₹375, which is not among the options at all (250/350/650/750). The keyed 750 is 30% of 2,500, so the percentage in the stem is wrong.
The fraction was lost in extraction: the stem prints 'x + 2 x + 3 > 1' where the original is (x+2)/(x+3) > 1. The keyed answer 0 is right for the original; the printed inequality is meaningless.
Garbled stem — not a question.
Orphaned passage fragment — 'in the context of boys/home/physical education' with no passage.
Orphaned passage fragment.
Orphaned passage fragment — 'in the context of boys/home/physical education' with no passage.
Incomplete stem — 'the principle' has no referent. Nothing to answer.
Garbled: options 1947/1950/1975/2000 with 1975 keyed. Not a coherent question.
Garbled stem ('air dock'), and one option is itself OCR garbage.
Stem is a mistranslation: it asks about climate change while the options are four 1919 dates (the real question was Jallianwala Bagh).

Key verified C = '14 मार्च', but Ambedkar was born 14 APRIL 1891 and '14 अप्रैल' is option B. The key matches the commission page, so the OPTION extraction is what is wrong. Either way the paper would mark a factually false date correct.
Refers to statements that are not printed.
Match-the-columns with NO columns printed — the lists did not survive extraction.
Spreadsheet/IT question. Computer knowledge is NOT in the Inter Level prelim syllabus — it is a separate technical eligibility requirement.

Stem and options do not correspond: '1857 ई. विद्रोह के कारणों में ?' (among the CAUSES of the 1857 revolt) with four PEOPLE as options. The original asked who led it in Bihar. One option is also garbled (सहजानंद गाधी).
'बहुउद्देशीय कंपनी' (multi-purpose company) where the original must be बहुराष्ट्रीय (multinational), and option A 'कोई मेटल्स' is OCR garbage rather than a company.
'What is not the essence of physical education?' with options Toys / Music / Sports / Education. Part of the same corrupted cluster as Q96-Q99 in this paper; the option set is not credible.

STALE CURRENT AFFAIRS. 'Who is the Vice-President of India?' keyed Jagdeep Dhankhar. Correct when the paper was set in 2025; he resigned in July 2025, so a 2026 student would be taught a wrong current fact. Present-tense office-holder questions must not be reused.
STALE CURRENT AFFAIRS. 'Who is the minister of External Affairs of India?' — present-tense office-holder question; correct only for the year it was set.
STALE CURRENT AFFAIRS. 'भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक के वर्तमान गवर्नर कौन हैं?' — explicitly asks for the CURRENT governor.
Garbled stem: 'राज्यसभा के सदस्य कौन है ?' has no determinate answer as printed.
Garbled Hindi stem ('कवि' के दांठ के कहानिकार कौन हैं?) — not a question.
Networking-protocol matching question (HTTP/FTP/SMTP/DNS). Computer knowledge is not in the Inter Level prelim syllabus, and the Purposes list did not survive extraction either.

The commission's key is D with the description '11 जनवरी, 2010', but OUR extracted option D reads '11 January, 2011' and option C reads '11 January, 2010'. The key is right and the OPTIONS are mis-extracted, so the paper would mark the wrong year correct. (JNNSM was launched 11 January 2010.)
'Match the Columns - G20 Countries and their Currencies' with neither column printed. Nothing to match.
'Which of the following is/are true regarding interest?' with options 'I only', 'II and IV only' etc but the statements themselves are absent.
'Which of the following statements about the Indian Rupee symbol are correct?' — the numbered statements are not printed, only the option combinations.

The correct answer is not among the options. '5, 11, 23, 47, ?' follows x2+1, giving 95; the options are 190/193/191/188 and the key is 191 — which is 95x2+1, the term AFTER the one asked for. A term was lost from the printed series.

The Hindi drops a person from the puzzle: 'A, B, C और E एक बेंच पर बैठे हुए हैं' where the English correctly says A, B, C, D and E. A Hindi-medium student is given a five-seat puzzle with four people and cannot solve it.
Malformed analogy stem: 'Pediatrics : Children :: ? : Geriatrics : ?' — two blanks and the pair inverted. The intended answer (Aged) is right, but the question as printed cannot be read.

excluded_sources.label: BSSC 8th Level 2024
excluded_sources.reason: EXCLUDED WHOLESALE. Seven of its 32 eligible questions were verified defective by working them — a 22% rate, against 0.8% for the Field Assistant paper. Since these defects are only findable by solving each question, a 22% measured rate implies more that have not been found. The paper contributes only 32 questions (7 of them Science/Maths), so keeping it buys little and risks a wrong answer in front of students.

_rules: STALE CURRENT AFFAIRS: never reuse a present-tense office-holder question ('who is the VP/CJI/minister/governor'). A date-anchored version is fine ('who became the 52nd CJI on 14 May 2025') because it stays true. This class cannot be caught by any structural check and does not show up as a defect in the source paper — it simply expires.
